Q7658956.label: Swiss federal salaries referendum, 1933
Q7658956.summary: A referendum on federal salaries was held in Switzerland on 28 May 1933. Voters were asked whether they approved of a federal law that would lower the salaries of federal officials on a temporary basis. The proposal was rejected by 55.1% of voters.

Q108711372.label: Referendum on expropriation in Berlin
Q108711372.summary: The 2021 Berlin referendum on a resolution to work out a draft for a law to expropriate housing stock of big housing companies, informally referred to as Deutsche Wohnen & Co. enteignen or DW enteignen, the main campaigning claim, was a referendum held and passed in Berlin in 2021.

Q84081612.label: May 2023 Greek parliamentary election
Q84081612.img: Greek elections 21 May 2023 ballot box c.jpg
Q84081612.summary: Snap parliamentary elections were held in Greece on 21 May 2023 to elect all 300 members of the Hellenic Parliament. They were the first elections since 1990 to be held without a seat bonus, due to amendments to the electoral law made in 2016. The elections instead used a system of proportional representation.

Q250828.label: Yasuhiro Nakasone
Q250828.summary: Yasuhiro Nakasone was a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 1982 to 1987. His political term was best known for pushing through the privatization of state-owned companies, pursuing a hawkish and pro-United States foreign policy and his rejection of Keynesianism and his support of neoliberalism.

Positions held: member of the House of Representatives of Japan

Q569292.label: 2007 Yazidi communities bombings
Q569292.desc: four coordinated suicide car bombings in northwestern Iraq
Q569292.summary: The Qahtaniyah bombings occurred on 14 August 2007, when four coordinated suicide car bomb attacks detonated in the Yazidi towns of Til Ezer (al-Qahtaniyah) and Siba Sheikh Khidir (al-Jazirah), in northern Iraq.

Q3269580.label: bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers
Q3269580.desc: financial collapse and Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing of American investment bank Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. and related entities during subprime mortgage crisis and great recession
Q3269580.summary: The bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, also known as the Crash of '08 and the Lehman Shock, on September 15, 2008, was the climax of the subprime mortgage crisis.

Q60774860.label: Maidan Shar attack
Q60774860.summary: On 21 January 2019, in central Afghanistan, the Taliban attacked a military compound in Maidan Shar, killing officers of the Afghan National Directorate of Security. The Taliban attacked while engaging in the process of negotiating a truce with the United States.

mentions.c: Afghanistan: Terrorist attack: Maidan Shar attack

Q5731788.label: Bombing of Tétouan
Q5731788.summary: On 18 July 1936 the Moroccan city of Tétouan was the target of an aerial bombardment, carried out by Spanish aircraft loyal to the Second Spanish Republic, barely hours after the beginning of the rebellion that triggered the Spanish Civil War.

Q16839116.label: Operations Ginny I and II
Q16839116.desc: 1944 failed sabotage missions during World War II
Q16839116.summary: Operations Ginny I and II were two ill-fated sabotage missions conducted by the U.S. Office of Strategic Services (OSS) in 1944 during the Italian campaign of World War II. Their aim was to blow up railway tunnels that would cut the line of communication to German forces in central Italy. The first mission, Ginny I, occurred on February 27/28, 1944, when fifteen U.S. soldiers attempted to land west of the small town of Framura. However, the OSS team had to abort after they landed on the wrong spot and could not find the tunnel.

Q134455244.label: Battle of Bhamdoun
Q134455244.summary: The Battle of Bhamdoun was fought over Bhamdoun between the Progressive Socialist Party (PSP) and the Lebanese Forces (LF) from 5 to 7 September 1983. It was the opening battle of the 1983 phase of the Lebanese Civil War and resulted in the successful capture of Bhamdoun by the Druze PLA militia.

Q46028.label: Mitrovdan offensive
Q46028.summary: Operation Bura, also known as the Mitrovdan Offensive, was a military operation conducted from 8 to 13 November 1992 during the Bosnian War. It took place in the area of Vranjevići near Nevesinje in eastern Herzegovina, where combined Croat–Bosniak forces attempted to break through the defensive lines of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS). The battle ended in a defensive victory for the VRS, which maintained control of the region and repelled the attacks.

Q7096780.label: Operation Badlands
Q7096780.summary: This is a list of coalition military operations of the Iraq War, undertaken by Multi-National Force – Iraq. The list covers operations from 2003 until December 2011. For later operations, see American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021).

Q55108044.label: 2018 Southern Syria offensive
Q55108044.summary: The 2018 Southern Syria offensive, code-named Operation Basalt, was a military operation launched by the Syrian Arab Army (SAA) and its allies against the rebels and ISIL in Southern Syria. The fighting began with a surprise attack on rebel-held areas in the eastern part of the Daraa Governorate in an attempt to fracture rebel-held lines and weaken morale, ahead of their offensive in the greater Southern Syria region.

Q110645708.label: Battle of Hasakah
Q110645708.summary: The Battle of Hasakah was a large-scale Islamic State attack and prison riot aimed at freeing arrested fighters of the Islamic State from al-Sina'a prison in the Ghuwayran (Geweran) area of Hasakah, Syria, which resulted in a SDF military victory and an ISIS prison break, with hundreds of prisoners, including important Emirs, being freed from captivity. The attack was the largest attack committed by the Islamic State since it lost its last key Syrian territory in 2019.

Q1563596.label: Social Democratic Party of Croatia and Slavonia
Q1563596.wiki: Social Democratic Party of Croatia and Slavonia
Q1563596.summary: The Social Democratic Party of Croatia and Slavonia was a social-democratic political party in the Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia. The party was active from 1894 until 1916.

Q49100.label: Yom Kippur War
Q49100.desc: October 1973 war between Egypt and Syria at one side and Israel on the other side
Q49100.summary: The Yom Kippur War, also known as the 1973 Arab–Israeli War, the fourth Arab–Israeli War, the October War, or the Ramadan War, was fought between Israel and a coalition of Arab states led by Egypt and Syria. Most of the fighting occurred in the Sinai Peninsula and the Golan Heights, territories occupied by Israel in 1967. Some combat also took place in mainland Egypt and northern Israel.
